chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Mis'mam, Abu Sayyar, who said:

He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Sayyar, the state of the Muhrim (one in Ihram) is restrictive. If he kisses his wife while not desiring (sexual release) and he is Muhrim, then upon him is the blood of a sheep. And if he kisses his wife while desiring and he ejaculates, then upon him is the blood of a camel, and he seeks forgiveness from Allah. And whoever touches his wife while Muhrim with desire, then upon him is the blood of a sheep. And whoever looks at his wife with desire and ejaculates, then upon him is the blood of a camel. And if he touches his wife and stays close to her without desire, then there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.أَبْنَى: He ejaculated (reached the point of seminal emission)
key_terms.جَزُور: The blood of a camel (a heavier financial sacrifice)
key_terms.دَمُ شَاة: The blood of a sheep (a type of financial sacrifice)
key_terms.لَازَمَهَا: He stayed close to her / maintained intimacy
key_terms.مُحْرِم: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific sacrifices required for a Muhrim who kisses or touches his wife during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s al-Ishtibār details the specific financial expiations (dam) for a pilgrim in Ihram who engages in intimacy with his wife, distinguishing between acts with and without sexual desire (shahwah) and the presence or absence of ejaculation. It prescribes a sheep (dam) for kissing or touching with desire without ejaculation, and a camel (jazoor) for acts leading to ejaculation, reflecting the juristic principle that the severity of the penalty correlates with the intensity of the pleasure and its consequence. This ruling highlights the nuanced Shia approach to Ihram violations, balancing the sanctity of the pilgrimage state with the natural human inclination.
